introduction_markdown: Time allowed: two and a half hours. Answer ALL questions. Section I is designed to be answered in 1 hour and Section II in 1 1/2 hours; you are advised to divide your time accordingly. In Section II answer EITHER the a, b and c OR the d, e and f of each question. For your guidance the approximate mark for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Where necessary, assume: the acceleration of free fall, $g = 10\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$; the speed of light in air, $c = 3\times10^{8}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$; the charge on an electron, $e = 1.6\times10^{-19}\,\mathrm{C}$. Calculators are allowed.

Identification retenue d'après le branchement : M1 est en série dans la boucle (ampèremètre) ; M2 est branché aux bornes de la résistance de 5 ohms (voltmètre). questions.enonce_markdown:
Figure 3 shows a network of resistors connected to a 12 V power source.

![fig-1](gce-ol-physics-2025-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_5_fig_1.png)

*Figure 3*

(i) Identify the meters $M_1$ and $M_2$. *[2 marks]*

(ii) State a property of each meter which makes it suitable for the connection as shown. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i)** $M_1$ is connected **in series** with the other components, so it is an **ammeter** (it measures the current in the circuit). $M_2$ is connected **in parallel** across the $5\,\Omega$ resistor, so it is a **voltmeter** (it measures the potential difference across that resistor).

**(ii)**

- The **ammeter** has a **very low (almost zero) resistance**, so that placing it in series does not reduce the current it is measuring.
- The **voltmeter** has a **very high resistance**, so that it draws almost no current from the circuit and does not change the potential difference it is measuring.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Determine:

(i) The combined resistance in the circuit. *[3 marks]*

(ii) The current in the circuit. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i)** The two $20\,\Omega$ resistors are in parallel:

$$\frac{1}{R_p} = \frac{1}{20} + \frac{1}{20} = \frac{2}{20} \quad\Rightarrow\quad R_p = 10\,\Omega$$

This combination is in series with the $5\,\Omega$ resistor (the meters are ideal and add no resistance):

$$R = 5\,\Omega + 10\,\Omega = 15\,\Omega$$

**The combined resistance is $15\,\Omega$.**

**(ii)** By Ohm's law:

$$I = \frac{V}{R} = \frac{12\,\mathrm{V}}{15\,\Omega} = 0.8\,\mathrm{A}$$

**The current in the circuit is $0.8\,\mathrm{A}$** (it is the reading of $M_1$; each $20\,\Omega$ resistor carries $0.4\,\mathrm{A}$ and the voltmeter $M_2$ reads $0.8 \times 5 = 4\,\mathrm{V}$).
